name: DESED: Domestic Environment Sound Event Detection Benchmark
description: DESED (Domestic Environment Sound Event Detection) is a benchmark for recognizing sound events in domestic environments using weak labels and synthetic audio mixtures (featured as DCASE Task 4). It comprises 10 domestic sound classes: alarm/bell, blender, cat, dog, dishes, frying, electric shaver/toothbrush, running water, speech, and vacuum cleaner. It incorporates real recordings from AudioSet (14,412 unlabelled in-domain, 1,578 weakly labelled train, 1,168 strongly labelled validation, and 692 public evaluation clips) together with a soundbank of 3,395 isolated background/foreground sound events and 2,584 pre-rendered synthetic domestic soundscapes with precise timestamp onset/offset annotations generated via Scaper.
